items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: I said to T-Bone in New York, I said, “I’m going to write a book about you.” ... I went out three different times, twice to be with T-Bone ... And the third time I went out for the memorial concert, which I helped to organize

ctx.x: Helen Oakley Dance has been involved in jazz since the 1930s. Born in Toronto in 1913, she moved to Chicago as a young woman to be closer to the hot jazz of the decade. Through her own initiative, she recorded Paul Mares, Jabbo Smith and Jess Stacey, and staged concerts with Count Basie and Benny Goodman. It was at one of these concerts that Benny was brought together with pianist Teddy Wilson, setting the stage for one of the most famous trios in jazz history. Helen enjoyed a long and fruitful relationship with…
Helen and Stanley currently reside in Vista, California. Helen was interviewed in San Diego, California on February 12, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: I said to T-Bone in New York, I said, “I’m going to write a book about you.” ... twice to be with T-Bone and Joe Turner and Eddie Cleanhead.

ctx.x: Congratulations. That’s great. I have a couple of more minutes, and then we’ll wrap up. I did want to mention the T-Bone Walker book. I think it must have been a great deal of work.

Well it was all a pleasure. T-Bone was another personality like Chick. He was a wonderful person, and of course he was a wonderful guitarist, and a wonderful singer. And Stanley and I, Stanley had a friend who sent him records and we first heard him when we were there. And I’ve always loved blues anyways. And so I said to T-Bone in New York, I said, “I’m going to write a book about you.” He never heard of such a thing. And so his wife, who’s still alive and very nice and very sweet, and I said well I’ll come out…
Tim, why don’t you flip that, and then I’ll just wrap this up.
